summary: Harvard geneticist George Church, a genuine pioneer of genome sequencing, spent decades overselling biotech dreams, taking Jeffrey Epstein's money, flirting with eugenics and co-founding Colossal Biosciences, whose 2025 dire wolf claims inflated gene-edited gray wolves into de-extinction.

evidence.note: Church born 1954 on MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa, raised in Clearwater
Colossal announced in September 2021 with a plan for mammoths by 2027
Epstein funding of Church's lab dated from 2005, contact continuing into 2014 and beyond
DNA data storage of his own book framed as a publicity stunt and overhyped
2012 book and 2015 interview propose cloning Neanderthals with a human surrogate
BGI opens an institute named for Church in Shenzhen in 2017; its eugenics-like staff rules
Digitate, the genetic matching dating venture he co-founded in 2019
advisory role at BioViva, an anti-aging gene therapy firm with offshore trials
Ben Lamm meets Church at his Boston lab and they found Colossal
Lamm describes plans to profit by selling conservation credits
Interior Secretary Burgum cites de-extinction to argue against the Endangered Species Act

notes: Primary theme: science-exploration (taxonomy lists de-extinction as an example); fraud-grift is the title's framing and was the alternative primary. Colossal kept secondary since the story is built around Church. Aubrey de Grey and the SENS sexual misconduct allegations get a few minutes but did not reach sexual-abuse as a theme. Main span starts at the 2005 Epstein funding and Personal Genome Project. CN rests on the BGI segment; Siberia rewilding is only a plan.
